definition_zh: 使受精；给……施肥；使肥沃
definition_en: to join a male and a female cell, or to add nutrients to soil, water or a growing medium
core_image: 一只手把肥料撒进田垄，另一只手在显微镜下把精子送到卵子旁边
scene: 果园里，工人用软毛刷把花粉从一株花移到另一株花的柱头上。 Growers fertilize the rows by hand when the bees are too few to do the work.
sceneCN: 这里 fertilize 指「使（花）受精、给花授粉」（第 5 个义项：人为把配子送到位）；句意为当蜜蜂太少、干不了这活时，种植者就人工给这几行花授粉。

pos.zh: 使受精；使受孕；给……施肥；使肥沃

senses.title: Add nutrients to soil
senses.definition: to add substances to soil so that crops grow better
senses.definitionCN: 向土壤添加物质，使作物长得更好
senses.example: They fertilize the vegetable beds every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年秋天给菜畦施肥。
senses.why: the -ize suffix means 'make', and the root means 'fruitful', so fertilize reads as 'make fruitful'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ize 意为「使」，词根意为「能结果的」，因此 fertilize 读作「使之结果」。

senses.title: Enrich a body of water
senses.definition: to add nutrients to a lake, pond or sea
senses.definitionCN: 向湖泊、池塘或海洋添加养分
senses.example: Farm runoff fertilizes the bay every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农场的径流每年春天给海湾带来养分。
senses.why: water is treated exactly like soil: something is added so that growth increases, whether wanted or not.
senses.whyCN: 水被完全当作土壤处理：加入某种东西使生长增加，无论这是否是想要的结果。

senses.title: Join a sperm with an egg
senses.definition: to cause a female reproductive cell to fuse with a male one
senses.definitionCN: 使雌性生殖细胞与雄性生殖细胞融合
senses.example: A single sperm fertilizes the egg within hours of ovulation.
senses.exampleCN: 排卵后数小时内，一枚精子使卵子受精。
senses.why: the verb takes the egg as its object and the sperm as its instrument, so the egg is what becomes fruitful.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词以卵为宾语、以精子为工具，因此变得「能结果」的是卵。

senses.title: Make a female animal pregnant
senses.definition: to cause a female animal to conceive, as in breeding
senses.definitionCN: 使雌性动物怀孕，如育种中所为
senses.example: The stallion fertilized eleven mares that season.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹公马在那个季节使十一匹母马受孕。
senses.why: in animal husbandry the outcome matters more than the cell event, so the verb stands for the whole successful mating.
senses.whyCN: 在畜牧中结果比细胞事件更重要，动词因此代表整个成功的交配过程。

senses.title: Move pollen to a flower
senses.definition: to bring pollen to the stigma of a flower, by hand or by a chosen insect
senses.definitionCN: 把花粉送到花的柱头上，靠人工或选定的昆虫
senses.example: Workers fertilize the vanilla flowers with a small wooden needle.
senses.exampleCN: 工人用小木针给香草花授粉。
senses.why: in flowering plants the pollen must arrive before fusion can happen, so the verb covers the delivery stage too.
senses.whyCN: 在开花植物中，花粉必须先到达才可能融合，因此这个动词也覆盖了投递阶段。

senses.title: Make land productive
senses.definition: to improve land so that it can support more growth
senses.definitionCN: 改良土地，使其能支撑更多生长
senses.example: Decades of flooding fertilized the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的洪水使这片三角洲变得肥沃。
senses.why: this sense drops the nutrient material and keeps only the result: land that bears more than before.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项去掉了养分材料，只保留结果：土地比从前结出更多东西。

senses.title: Enrich the mind or imagination
senses.titleCN: 比喻：丰富、激发思想与想像
senses.definition: to supply something that makes a mind or a plan more productive
senses.definitionCN: 提供某种东西，使头脑或计划更有产出
senses.example: Travel fertilized her imagination more than any classroom did.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行比任何课堂都更能激发她的想像力。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the soil gesture to thought: an outside substance is added and growth follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把给土壤的动作移到思想上：加入外在之物，随后便有生长。

senses.title: Feed a laboratory medium
senses.definition: to add nutrients to a medium in which cells or plants are grown
senses.definitionCN: 向培养细胞或植物的介质中添加养分
senses.example: The team fertilized the culture medium with trace minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 团队向培养基中添加微量元素。
senses.why: a medium is a manufactured soil, so the agricultural verb fits it without any change of sense.
senses.whyCN: 培养基是人造的土壤，因此农业动词原样适用，词义不需改变。

intro.en: Fertilize comes from Medieval Latin fertilizare, built on fertilis 'fruitful', itself ferre 'to bear' plus -ilis 'able'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fertilize 来自中世纪拉丁 fertilizare，建立在 fertilis「能结果的」之上，后者由 ferre「承载」加 -ilis「能够」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre 'to bear, carry' is the source of fertile as well as of transfer and refer.
items.cn: ferre「承载、生育」既是 fertile 的来源，也是 transfer 与 refer 的来源。

items.en: Fertilis 'fruitful' is generally explained as ferre plus -ilis, 'able to bear'; the intermediate adjective is not attested in surviving texts.
items.cn: fertilis「能结果的」一般解释为 ferre 加 -ilis「能够承载」；这个中间形容词在现存文献中没有书证。

items.en: Fertilizare meant 'to make fruitful' and was applied to land long before it was applied to gametes.
items.cn: fertilizare 意为「使之结果」，用于土地远早于用于配子。

items.en: English fertilize appears in the seventeenth century in agricultural writing, then spreads to biology in the eighteenth and nineteenth.
items.cn: 英语 fertilize 于 17 世纪出现在农业写作中，18、19 世纪扩展到生物学。

items.en: Source uncertain (first biological date): the first use of the verb for the union of gametes is not precisely dated; the agricultural record is clearer than the biological one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（生物学义的首见年代）：这个动词首次用于配子结合的时间没有确切记载；农业用法的记录比生物学用法更清楚。

note.en: Group one separates the -fer- verbs that differ only by prefix; group two separates verbs of supplying from verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组区分只靠前缀不同的 -fer- 动词；第二组区分「供给」类动词与「结合」类动词。

entries.definition: From Latin fermentum 'leaven', not from ferre; it means to break down sugars, so the shared fer- is a coincidence of spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fermentum「酵素」，并非出自 ferre；意为分解糖分，因此相同的 fer- 只是拼写巧合。

entries.definition: From Latin fomentum 'a warm application'; it means to stir up trouble or apply warmth, with no link to fertility.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fomentum「热敷物」；意为煽动或热敷，与肥沃无关。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus ferre: to bring together in speech, hence to consult or bestow.
entries.definitionCN: con-「一起」加 ferre：在言语中带到一处，因此指商议或授予。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus ferre: to carry something away to a later time, hence to postpone.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 ferre：把某事搬到以后的时间，因此指推迟。

entries.definition: To supply what a living thing needs to grow; it names the feeding, while fertilize names making the medium fruitful.
entries.definitionCN: 提供生物生长所需之物；它指喂养，而 fertilize 指使介质变得肥沃。

entries.definition: To transfer pollen to a stigma; this is the delivery step, while fertilize covers the fusion that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 把花粉送到柱头；这是投递步骤，而 fertilize 覆盖其后的融合。

entries.definition: To introduce semen into the reproductive tract by technical means; fertilization may follow or may not.
entries.definitionCN: 用技术手段把精液送入生殖道；之后可能受精，也可能不受精。

entries.definition: A general verb for adding value or nutrients; it lacks the specific 'bearing fruit' image of fertilize.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指增加价值或养分；缺少 fertilize 那种「结果实」的具体意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real farm and lab phrases, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的农事与实验搭配以及真实同族词。

normal.en: fer- 'bear' + -tilis 'able' + -ize 'make': to make able to bear.
normal.cn: fer-「承载」+ -tilis「能够」+ -ize「使」：使能够承载、结果。

normal.en: Soil, water, eggs, flowers and culture media can all take the same verb.
normal.cn: 土壤、水、卵、花与培养基都能接受同一个动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fertilize the soil, fertilize an egg, fertilize with manure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：给土壤施肥、使卵受精、用厩肥施肥。

normal.en: The noun pair is regular: fertilize gives fertilization, as -ize gives -ization.
normal.cn: 名词配对很规则：fertilize 派生 fertilization，正如 -ize 派生 -ization。

normal.en: The family runs fertile, fertility, fertilizer, fertilization, self-fertilize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fertile、fertility、fertilizer、fertilization、self-fertilize。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tipping a jar of richness into a field of thin soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一罐养分倒进贫瘠的田里。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener carrying pollen on a brush as if delivering a letter.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁用刷子带着花粉，像在投递一封信。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that reads widely and then produces ideas it could not produce before.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广泛阅读的头脑，随后产出它原本产不出的想法。

examples.en: Farmers fertilize the fields before the spring rains.
examples.cn: 农民在春雨之前给田地施肥。

examples.en: The bees fertilize the apple trees as they gather nectar.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂采蜜时给苹果树授粉。

examples.en: Too much runoff fertilized the pond and choked it with weeds.
examples.cn: 过多的径流给池塘带来了养分，杂草因此疯长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fer（带来）+ til（能够）+ ize（使）」——使卵子或土地能够结果 → 使受精、施肥

root: 拉丁 fertilis「能结果的」= ferre「承载、生育」+ -ilis「能够」；中世纪拉丁 fertilizare「使结果」；英语 fertilize。ferre 的印欧来源一般认为是 *bher-，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fertilize all perform one act: something is supplied or brought together so that growth becomes possible.
sensesIntro.cn: fertilize 的八个义项都在做同一件事：供给或促成结合，使生长成为可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of richness dropped into a medium that could not otherwise bear much.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把养分落进原本长不出多少东西的介质。

branches.en: FEEDING A MEDIUM: soil, water and culture medium are all enriched the same way.
branches.cn: 喂养介质：土壤、水与培养基都以同样方式被加料。

branches.en: JOINING LIVES: one cell meets another, with conception as the animal result.
branches.cn: 生命的结合：一个细胞遇见另一个，在动物身上便成为受孕。

branches.en: DELIVERY FIRST: pollen has to arrive before any fusion can occur.
branches.cn: 先投递：花粉必须先到，融合才可能发生。

branches.en: RESULT WITHOUT MATERIAL: land can simply become more productive.
branches.cn: 无料之果：土地可以只是变得更能出产。

branches.en: MIND AS SOIL: thought is enriched by what is brought in from outside.
branches.cn: 以心为土：思想因外来之物而变得肥沃。

intro.en: Fertilize is a Latin root plus two suffixes, and its family covers farming, biology and medicine.
intro.cn: fertilize 是拉丁词根加两个后缀，其词族覆盖农业、生物学与医学。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre 'to bear' yields fertilis and fertilizare; English adds fertilize, fertilizer, fertilization and the wider -fer- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ferre「承载」衍生 fertilis 与 fertilizare；英语再加上 fertilize、fertilizer、fertilization 以及更广的 -fer- 词族。

definition_zh: 纤维；纤维材料；膳食纤维；品格
definition_en: a thin thread-like part of a material, the part of food that helps digestion, or strength of character

scene: 她把麻绳捻开，露出一缕缕细丝。The rope is made of natural fibre.

definition_zh: 小说；虚构作品；编造的说法

definition_zh: 田地；领域；场地；战场；派上场
definition_en: an area of land for crops, a subject of study, a sports ground, a battlefield, or to send players into a game

abstract.cn: 不出一拳也能赢得一场斗争。

abstract.en: What we fight for shows who we are.

abstract.en: Fighting spirit outlasts a single battle.
abstract.cn: 斗志比一场战役更长久。

core.en: Force meeting force.

branches.en: Two people trading blows.

The pilots were locked in a dogfight.

definition_zh: 数字；人物；图形；身材；认为
definition_en: a number or amount, a well-known person, a shape or diagram, a body shape, or to think or calculate
core_image: 纸上画着一个简单的火柴人，旁边写着一串数字
scene: 图表上的数字稳步上升。The figures show a steady rise.
sceneCN: 这里 figures 是「数字」（第 1 个义项）；句意：图表上的数字稳步上升。

senses.title: Number
senses.definition: a number or amount shown in data
senses.definitionCN: 数据中显示的数字或数量
senses.example: The figures show a steady rise.
senses.exampleCN: 图表上的数字稳步上升。
senses.why: Numbers are the most common written figure.
senses.whyCN: 数字是最常见的书写形式之一。

senses.title: Person
senses.definition: a well-known or important person
senses.definitionCN: 知名或重要的人
senses.example: She is a public figure.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位公众人物。
senses.why: A person can stand out as a figure.
senses.whyCN: 人可以因出众而成为一个重要人物。

senses.title: Shape
senses.definition: a shape, diagram, or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 形状、图形或图案
senses.example: The figure in the corner is a triangle.
senses.exampleCN: 角上的图形是一个三角形。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of form.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语中形状的本义。

senses.title: Body shape
senses.definition: the shape of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 人的体形
senses.example: He watches his figure.
senses.exampleCN: 他很注意保持身材。
senses.why: The body is a shape people care about.
senses.whyCN: 身体是人们在意的一种形状。

senses.title: To work out
senses.definition: to think, calculate, or conclude
senses.definitionCN: 思考、计算或推断
senses.example: I figure it will rain today.
senses.exampleCN: 我估计今天会下雨。
senses.why: To figure is to give a thought its shape.
senses.whyCN: 推断就是给想法一个形状。

intro.en: Figure comes from Latin figura, a shape, from fingere, to form.
intro.cn: figure 出自拉丁语 figura（形状），源于 fingere（塑造）。

items.en: Fingere meant to shape or mould.
items.cn: fingere 意为塑造或模制。

items.en: Figura named the shape that results.
items.cn: figura 指塑造出的形状。

items.en: Old French figure carried the sense of form and face.
items.cn: 古法语 figure 兼具外形与面容之意。

items.en: English figure added numbers and persons.
items.cn: 英语 figure 增加了数字与人物之义。

items.en: Figure out means to solve or understand.
items.cn: figure out 意为解决或弄明白。

note.en: Figure is compared with similar-looking words and with words for its main senses.
note.cn: 把 figure 与形近词以及表示其主要义项的词作比较。

entries.definition: a leader with no real power

normalIntro.en: Figure runs from a drawn shape to a number, a person, and a way of thinking.
normalIntro.cn: figure 从画出的形状延伸到数字、人物和思考方式。

normal.en: Sales figures show how a shop is doing.
normal.cn: 销售数字显示店铺经营状况。

normal.en: A public figure is often in the news.
normal.cn: 公众人物常出现在新闻里。

normal.en: Figure out means to find the answer.
normal.cn: figure out 意为找到答案。

normal.en: A figure can be a drawing in a book.
normal.cn: figure 可以是书中的插图。

normal.en: She keeps her figure by walking.
normal.cn: 她靠走路保持身材。

abstract.en: A shape becomes a number once we count it.
abstract.cn: 一旦我们去数，形状就变成数字。

abstract.en: A person can be a figure in history.
abstract.cn: 一个人可以成为历史中的一个人物。

abstract.en: To figure is to give shape to a thought.
abstract.cn: 去推断，就是给想法一个形状。

examples.en: The figures show a steady rise.
examples.cn: 图表上的数字稳步上升。

examples.en: She is a public figure.
examples.cn: 她是一位公众人物。

examples.en: I figure it will rain today.
examples.cn: 我估计今天会下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: figure 出自拉丁语 figura（形状），本义「塑造出的形态」，由图形扩展到数字、人物、身材与推断。

root: 源自拉丁语 figura（形状），出自 fingere（塑造），核心义「成形的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Figure means a number, a person, a shape, a body form, or to think and calculate.
sensesIntro.cn: figure 意为数字、人物、图形、身材，或认为与估算。

core.en: A form that can be seen, counted, or thought about.
core.cn: 可以被看见、被计数或被思考的形态。

branches.en: Data expressed as numbers.
A person who stands out.

intro.en: Figure belongs to the Latin family of shaping and form.
intro.cn: figure 属于拉丁语中表示塑造与形状的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin figura and fingere are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figura 与 fingere 是历史词根。

items.example: The president is only a figurehead.
items.exampleCN: 这位总统只是名义领袖。
那个故事是臆造出来的。

definition_zh: 电影；胶片；薄膜；拍摄
definition_en: a motion picture, a thin strip of material for recording images, a thin layer, or to record something with a camera
core_image: 放映机的光穿过胶片，在墙上投出晃动的画面
scene: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。We watched a film about the ocean last night.
sceneCN: 这里 film 是「电影」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

senses.title: Motion picture
senses.definition: a story or record shown in moving pictures
senses.definitionCN: 以活动画面讲述故事或记录事物的作品
senses.example: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Photographic strip
senses.definition: a thin strip coated to record images
senses.definitionCN: 涂有感光层、用于记录影像的薄带
senses.example: The old camera still uses film.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。
senses.why: Moving pictures were once recorded on film.
senses.whyCN: 活动画面曾被记录在胶片上。

senses.title: Thin layer
senses.definition: a very thin layer of material
senses.definitionCN: 一层极薄的材料
senses.example: A film of oil covered the water.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上覆着一层油膜。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a thin skin or layer.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是薄皮或薄层。

senses.title: To record
senses.definition: to record something with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用摄影机记录某物
senses.example: They filmed the whole ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拍摄了整场仪式。
senses.why: The material name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 材料名转化为动作。

intro.en: Film comes from Old English filmen, a thin skin or membrane.
intro.cn: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜）。

items.en: Filmen meant a thin skin or membrane.
items.cn: filmen 意为薄皮或薄膜。

items.en: Film named a thin covering or haze.
items.cn: film 指薄薄的覆盖层或薄雾。

items.en: Photography gave film a light-sensitive strip.
items.cn: 摄影术使 film 指感光胶片。

items.en: Film came to mean a motion picture.
items.cn: film 进而指电影。

items.en: The verb means to record with a camera.
items.cn: 动词形式意为用摄影机拍摄。

note.en: Film is compared with similar-looking words and with words for movies and layers.
note.cn: 把 film 与形近词以及表示电影和薄层的词作比较。

entries.definition: the art or place of films
a thin layer over a surface

normalIntro.en: Film is a thin layer first, then a strip that carries pictures, then the pictures themselves.
normalIntro.cn: film 先是薄层，再是承载画面的胶片，最后指影片本身。

normal.en: A film can mean a movie.
normal.cn: film 可以指一部电影。

normal.en: Old cameras used film.
normal.cn: 旧相机使用胶片。

normal.en: Soap leaves a film on the glass.
normal.cn: 肥皂在玻璃上留下一层薄膜。

normal.en: The verb means to record.
normal.cn: 动词形式意为拍摄。

normal.en: A filmmaker makes films.
normal.cn: filmmaker 拍电影。

abstract.en: A thin layer can hold a whole world of light.
abstract.cn: 薄薄一层也能承载整个光的世界。

abstract.en: Pictures in motion turn time into a story.
abstract.cn: 活动的画面把时间变成故事。

abstract.en: Recording is a way of refusing to forget.
abstract.cn: 记录是一种拒绝遗忘的方式。

examples.en: We watched a film about the ocean last night.
examples.cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于海洋的电影。

examples.en: The old camera still uses film.
examples.cn: 这台旧相机仍使用胶片。

examples.en: A film of oil covered the water.
examples.cn: 水面上覆着一层油膜。

dict_mnemonic.text: film 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮），本义「薄层」，后指感光胶片，再指电影与拍摄。

root: 源自古英语 filmen（薄皮、薄膜），核心义「薄薄的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Film means a movie, a photographic strip, a thin layer, or to record with a camera.
sensesIntro.cn: film 意为电影、胶片、薄膜或拍摄。

core.en: A thin layer that can carry images.
core.cn: 能承载影像的薄层。

branches.en: A story told in moving pictures.
branches.cn: 用活动画面讲述的故事。

branches.en: A strip that holds images.
A very thin covering.
The act of recording.
The strip and the recording share one word.
branches.cn: 胶片与拍摄共用一个词。

intro.en: Film belongs to the old Germanic family of thin coverings.
intro.cn: film 属于日耳曼语中表示薄覆盖层的古老词族。

latinIntro.en: Film has no Latin ancestor; Latin pellicula, a thin skin, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: film 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pellicula（薄皮）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 这位电影制作人获奖了。

items.example: The scene has a filmic quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景有电影般的质感。

items.example: The records are stored on microfilm.
items.exampleCN: 这些记录存放在缩微胶片上。

definition_zh: 过滤器；滤光片；过滤；筛选
definition_en: a device that removes unwanted matter, a screen that changes light, to pass something through such a device, or to screen information
core_image: 咖啡一滴一滴穿过滤纸，落进下面的玻璃壶
scene: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
sceneCN: 这里 filter 是「过滤器」（第 1 个义项）；句意：咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

senses.title: Straining device
senses.definition: a device that removes unwanted matter from liquid or air
senses.definitionCN: 从液体或空气中除去杂质的装置
senses.example: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。
senses.why: This is the basic device sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的装置义。

senses.title: Light screen
senses.definition: a screen that lets some light through and blocks the rest
senses.definitionCN: 让部分光通过而挡住其余光的镜片
senses.example: The photographer put a filter on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在镜头上装了滤光片。
senses.why: The device sense extends to light.
senses.whyCN: 装置义扩展到光线。

senses.title: To strain
senses.definition: to pass liquid or air through a filter
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或空气通过过滤器
senses.example: They filter the water before drinking it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们喝水前先过滤。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To screen
senses.definition: to remove unwanted information or people
senses.definitionCN: 剔除不需要的信息或人员
senses.example: The software filters spam from email.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。
senses.why: Filtering applies to data as well as liquid.
senses.whyCN: 过滤也适用于数据，而不只是液体。

intro.en: Filter comes from Medieval Latin filtrum, felt, used as a strainer, through Old French filtre.
intro.cn: filter 出自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），因毛毡可用作滤材，经古法语 filtre 而来。

items.en: Filtrum meant felt used for straining.
items.cn: filtrum 指用于过滤的毛毡。

items.en: Filtre meant a strainer.
items.cn: filtre 意为过滤器。

items.en: Filter named a cloth or device for straining.
items.cn: 英语 filter 指过滤用布或装置。

items.en: Filters also treat air and engine fuel.
items.cn: 过滤器也用于处理空气与发动机燃料。

items.en: The verb extends to screening information.
items.cn: 动词形式扩展到筛选信息。

note.en: Filter is compared with similar-looking words and with words for straining and screening.
note.cn: 把 filter 与形近词以及表示过滤和筛选的词作比较。

entries.definition: something used to fill a space
liquid that has passed a filter
a device for separating solids from liquid
a mesh for separating fine matter

normalIntro.en: A filter lets what is wanted through and holds back the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 过滤器让需要的东西通过，把其余部分留下。

normal.en: A coffee filter holds the grounds.
normal.cn: 咖啡滤纸拦住咖啡渣。

normal.en: An air filter keeps dust out.
normal.cn: 空气过滤器挡住灰尘。

normal.en: Filter out means to remove.
normal.cn: filter out 意为滤除。

normal.en: The noun and verb look the same.
normal.cn: 名词与动词形式相同。

normal.en: A filtrate is what passes through.
normal.cn: filtrate 是透过滤器的液体。

abstract.en: To filter is to choose what may pass.
abstract.cn: 过滤就是选择什么可以通过。

abstract.en: Attention is a filter for a noisy world.
abstract.cn: 注意力是应对喧闹世界的过滤器。

abstract.en: What is held back can be as important as what gets through.
abstract.cn: 被挡住的东西可以和通过的一样重要。

examples.en: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
examples.cn: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

examples.en: They filter the water before drinking it.
examples.cn: 他们喝水前先过滤。

examples.en: The software filters spam from email.
examples.cn: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。

core.cn: 挑选何物可通过的屏障。

branches.en: A device for liquid or air.

branches.en: A screen for light.

intro.en: Filter belongs to the Medieval Latin filtrum family of straining.
intro.cn: filter 属于中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡）词族，关联过滤。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin filtrum is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 filtrum 是历史词根。

definition_zh: 金融；财政；资金；为……提供资金
definition_en: the management of money, public revenue, the money needed for a project, or to provide money for something
core_image: 账本上一列数字被红笔圈出，旁边写着收支平衡
scene: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。The company needs finance to expand production.
sceneCN: 这里 finance 是「资金」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。

senses.title: Money management
senses.definition: the management of money and investment
senses.definitionCN: 对货币与投资的管理
senses.example: She works in finance.
senses.exampleCN: 她从事金融工作。
senses.why: This is the broad field sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是广义领域义。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: the money and spending of a government
senses.definitionCN: 政府的收入与支出
senses.example: Public finance pays for roads and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 公共财政支付道路与学校。
senses.why: The field sense narrows to government.
senses.whyCN: 领域义缩小到政府。

senses.title: Funds
senses.definition: the money needed for a project
senses.definitionCN: 项目所需的钱
senses.example: The company needs finance to expand production.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司需要资金来扩大生产。
senses.why: Money for a purpose is finance.

senses.title: To fund
senses.definition: to provide money for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事提供资金
senses.example: The city financed the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府为新桥提供资金。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of providing money.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为提供资金的动作。

intro.cn: finance 出自中古法语 finance（清偿债务），源于 finer（了结），再追溯到拉丁语 finis（终点）。

items.en: Finis meant end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或界限。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finer 意为了结债务。

items.en: Finance named the settling of money matters.
items.cn: finance 指钱财事务的了结。

items.en: Finance named the management of money.
items.cn: finance 指对金钱的管理。

items.en: It also became a verb meaning to fund.
items.cn: 它也变成动词，意为提供资金。

note.en: Finance is compared with similar-looking words and with words for money matters.
note.cn: 把 finance 与形近词以及表示钱财事务的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who manages large sums
coins and notes used to pay

normalIntro.en: Finance is money managed, money raised, and money provided.
normalIntro.cn: finance 是被管理的钱、被筹集的资金与被提供的款项。

normal.en: Finance began with settling debts.
normal.cn: finance 最初与了结债务有关。

normal.en: Public finance belongs to the state.
normal.cn: 公共财政属于国家。

normal.en: A project needs finance to start.
normal.cn: 项目需要资金才能启动。

normal.en: To finance is to pay for something.
normal.cn: to finance 意为为某事出钱。

normal.en: The adjective is financial.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 financial。

abstract.cn: 钱是储存起来的劳动，从一只手流到另一只手。

abstract.en: A budget is a promise about the future.
abstract.cn: 预算是一份关于未来的承诺。

abstract.en: What a society funds shows what it values.

core.en: Money brought under control and put to use.

branches.en: The field that manages money.
The state's income and spending.
Money gathered for a purpose.

branches.en: The act of paying for something.
The field and the funds share one name.
branches.cn: 领域与资金共用一个名称。

intro.en: Finance belongs to the Latin finis family of settling and ending.
intro.cn: finance 属于拉丁语 finis（终点）词族，关联了结与结算。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与法语 finer 是历史词根。

definition_zh: 金融的；财政的；财务的
definition_en: relating to money, banking, or the management of funds
core_image: 银行大厅的屏幕上，一排排数字不停地跳动
scene: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。The company is in financial trouble.
sceneCN: 这里 financial 是「财务的」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家公司正陷入财务困境。

senses.title: Banking and investment
senses.definition: relating to banks, investments, and money markets
senses.definitionCN: 与银行、投资和货币市场有关的
senses.example: She works in the financial sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在金融行业工作。
senses.why: This sense points to banks and investment.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指向银行与投资领域。

senses.title: Public revenue
senses.definition: relating to the money of a government
senses.definitionCN: 与政府收支有关的
senses.example: The city faces a financial shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临财政短缺。
senses.why: Governments also manage money.
senses.whyCN: 政府同样要管理资金。

senses.title: Company accounts
senses.definition: relating to the money and accounts of a business
senses.definitionCN: 与企业的资金和账目有关的
senses.example: The company is in financial trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。
senses.why: A business keeps its own accounts.
senses.whyCN: 企业有自己的账目要管。

intro.en: Financial goes back to Latin finis, an end, through French finance, a payment that settles a debt.

items.en: Finis meant an end or a boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finare meant to settle a debt.
items.cn: finare 意为结清债务。

items.en: Finance named a payment or revenue.
items.cn: finance 指付款或收入。

items.en: Finance came to mean money management.
items.cn: finance 进而指资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial described money matters.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述资金事务。

note.en: Financial is compared with similar-looking words and with words about money.

entries.definition: a person who deals in money

normalIntro.en: Financial is the adjective of finance, so it describes anything that involves money.
normalIntro.cn: financial 是 finance 的形容词，用来描述一切与金钱有关的事物。

normal.en: A financial crisis shakes the banks.
normal.cn: 金融危机让银行动荡。

normal.en: Financial aid helps students pay fees.
normal.cn: 经济援助帮学生支付学费。

normal.en: A financial adviser plans your money.
normal.cn: 理财顾问为你的钱做规划。

normal.en: The company reports financial results each year.
normal.cn: 公司每年公布财务业绩。

normal.en: Financial trouble means the money is short.
normal.cn: 财务困境意味着资金短缺。

abstract.en: Money is a promise that people agree to trust.
abstract.cn: 金钱是人们约定去信任的一种承诺。

abstract.en: A financial system turns trust into numbers.
abstract.cn: 金融体系把信任变成了数字。

abstract.en: Every account is a story of choices made.
abstract.cn: 每一本账目都是选择的故事。

examples.en: The company is in financial trouble.
examples.cn: 这家公司正陷入财务困境。

examples.en: She works in the financial sector.
examples.cn: 她在金融行业工作。

examples.en: They offered financial support to the family.
examples.cn: 他们向这家人提供了资金支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: financial 来自 finance（金融），加形容词后缀 -ial，表示「与资金有关的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经法语 finance（结算、收入）演变为「财政、金融」。

sensesIntro.en: Financial describes matters of banking, public revenue, or company accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: financial 描述银行、政府收支或企业账目方面的事务。

core.en: Everything that belongs to money and its management.
core.cn: 一切属于金钱及其管理的事物。

branches.en: Belonging to banks and investment.
Belonging to government money.
Belonging to a company's accounts.
Both deal with large sums of money.
Public and private books share the word.

intro.en: Financial is built from the noun finance plus the adjective suffix -ial.
intro.cn: financial 由名词 finance 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root finis, an end, also gave finish and final.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 finis（结束）也孕育了 finish 与 final。

items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

latinEntries.example: Finis marks the end of a debt.
Finare meant to end a debt by paying.
latinEntries.exampleCN: finare 意为付款了结债务。

definition_zh: 找到；发现；认为；裁决
definition_en: to discover something by searching, to come upon something, to consider something to be a certain way, or to make a legal decision
core_image: 手伸进沙发缝里，摸到那串丢失的钥匙
scene: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 find 是「找到」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

senses.title: To locate by searching
senses.definition: to discover something you have been looking for
senses.definitionCN: 找到一直在寻找的东西
senses.example: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of searching.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常生活中搜寻的义项。

senses.title: To come upon
senses.definition: to discover something without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 无意中遇到或发现某物
senses.example: We found a small café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: Some things are found by chance.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西是偶然发现的。

senses.title: To consider
senses.definition: to feel or think that something is a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 觉得或认为某事是某种样子
senses.example: I find this book very useful.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得这本书很有用。
senses.why: Experience shapes our judgment.
senses.whyCN: 经历会影响我们的判断。

senses.title: To decide a case
senses.definition: to make a legal decision about a case
senses.definitionCN: 对案件作出法律裁定
senses.example: The jury found him innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团裁定他无罪。
senses.why: A court also reaches a finding.
senses.whyCN: 法庭也会给出裁断。

intro.en: Find comes from Old English findan, to come upon, and has kept that core meaning for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），一千多年来一直保留着这个核心含义。

items.en: Findan meant to come upon something.
items.cn: findan 意为遇到某物。

items.en: The verb also covered opinion and judgment.
items.cn: 这个动词也包含看法与判断。

items.en: Found became the past tense.
items.cn: found 成为过去式。

items.en: Find out extended the idea of discovery.
items.cn: find out 扩展了发现的含义。

items.en: Legal use named the verdict of a court.
items.cn: 法律用法指法庭的裁断。

note.en: Find is compared with similar-looking words and with words for discovery.
note.cn: 把 find 与形近词以及表示发现的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside
to learn or notice for the first time
to find the exact place of

normalIntro.en: Find is the plain verb for coming upon something, whether by search or by chance.
normalIntro.cn: find 是表示遇到某物的基本动词，无论靠寻找还是靠偶然。

normal.en: You find what you look for.
normal.cn: 你寻找的东西会被你找到。

normal.en: We found a café by chance.
normal.cn: 我们偶然发现了一家咖啡馆。

normal.en: Find out means to learn a fact.
normal.cn: find out 意为查明一个事实。

normal.en: A jury can find a person innocent.
normal.cn: 陪审团可以裁定一个人无罪。

normal.en: The past tense of find is found.
normal.cn: find 的过去式是 found。

abstract.en: To find is to close the distance between wanting and having.
abstract.cn: 找到，就是缩短渴望与拥有之间的距离。

abstract.en: Some discoveries arrive without a search.
abstract.cn: 有些发现并不需要寻找。

abstract.en: What we find often changes what we were looking for.
abstract.cn: 我们找到的东西，常常改变我们原本寻找的东西。

examples.en: She found the lost keys behind the sofa.
examples.cn: 她在沙发后面找到了丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: We found a small café near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近发现了一家小咖啡馆。

examples.en: I find this book very useful.
examples.cn: 我觉得这本书很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: find 源自古英语 findan（遇到），不规则变化为 find、found、found。

root: 源自古英语 findan（遇到、发现），核心义「遇见并得到」。

sensesIntro.en: Find means to locate, to come upon, to consider, or to give a legal decision.
sensesIntro.cn: find 意为找到、发现、认为或作出裁决。

core.en: To come upon something or someone.
core.cn: 遇到某物或某人。

branches.en: To locate after searching.
To meet something by chance.
To form an opinion.
To reach a legal verdict.
Chance and judgment both begin with meeting.
branches.cn: 偶然与判断都始于遇见。

intro.en: Find is a native Germanic verb with a strong and irregular past tense.
intro.cn: find 是日耳曼语本族动词，过去式强变化且不规则。

latinIntro.en: Find has no Latin ancestor; Latin invenire, to come upon, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: find 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 invenire（遇到）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She finds new ideas every day.
items.exampleCN: 她每天都能发现新想法。

items.meaningCN: 找到（过去式与过去分词）

items.exampleCN: 找到答案花了几个小时。

items.example: The findings were published last week.

items.exampleCN: 他带着新获得的自信说话。

items.example: The file is findable by name.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件可以按名称找到。

definition_zh: 完成；结束；终点；表面处理
definition_en: to complete something, to come to an end, the end of something, or a surface treatment
core_image: 笔尖在最后一题上停住，试卷被轻轻合上
scene: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。She finished the last question and put down her pen.
sceneCN: 这里 finish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

senses.title: To complete
senses.definition: to bring a task or activity to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把任务或活动做到结尾
senses.example: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
senses.exampleCN: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的日常义项。

senses.title: To come to an end
senses.definition: to stop or end, especially at a planned time
senses.definitionCN: 停止或结束，尤指在预定时间结束
senses.example: The meeting finished at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在中午结束。
senses.why: Events as well as tasks can finish.
senses.whyCN: 不只是任务，事件也会结束。

senses.title: The end of a race
senses.definition: the last part or end of something, such as a race
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最后部分或终点，如比赛的终点
senses.example: The race had a close finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛的最后阶段竞争激烈。
senses.why: The noun names the ending point.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指结束的那个点。

senses.title: Surface treatment
senses.definition: the way a surface is treated or coated
senses.definitionCN: 表层的处理方式或涂层
senses.example: The table has a smooth finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子表面很光滑。
senses.why: A finished surface is the last stage of making.
senses.whyCN: 表面处理是制作过程的最后一步。

intro.en: Finish comes from Latin finis, an end, through Old French finir, to bring to an end.
intro.cn: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir（使结束）传入英语。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界。

items.en: Finir meant to bring to an end.
items.cn: finir 意为使某事结束。

items.en: Finishen meant to complete.
items.cn: finishen 意为完成。

items.en: Finish named the end of a race.
items.cn: finish 指比赛的终点。

items.en: Finish also named a surface treatment.
items.cn: finish 又指表面处理。

note.en: Finish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for completing.
note.cn: 把 finish 与形近词以及表示完成的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bring something to a close

normalIntro.en: Finish moves from doing the last step to naming the last point.
normalIntro.cn: finish 从做最后一步，延伸到命名最后那个点。

normal.en: Finish your homework before dinner.
normal.cn: 晚饭前把作业做完。

normal.en: The film finishes at nine.
normal.cn: 电影九点结束。

normal.en: The finish line is close.
normal.cn: 终点线就在眼前。

normal.en: A smooth finish makes wood shine.
normal.cn: 光滑的表面处理让木头发亮。

normal.en: Add a finishing touch to the cake.
normal.cn: 给蛋糕加上最后的点缀。

abstract.en: Every ending is also a boundary drawn in time.
abstract.cn: 每一个结束，也是在时间里画下的一道边界。

abstract.en: To finish is to decide that enough has been done.
abstract.cn: 完成，就是决定已经做得足够。

abstract.en: The last touch often reveals the whole craft.
abstract.cn: 最后一步，往往显露整门手艺。

examples.en: She finished the last question and put down her pen.
examples.cn: 她答完最后一题，放下了笔。

examples.en: The meeting finished at noon.
examples.cn: 会议在中午结束。

examples.en: The table has a smooth finish.
examples.cn: 这张桌子表面很光滑。

dict_mnemonic.text: finish 源自拉丁语 finis（结束），经古法语 finir 进入英语，核心义「做到尽头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 finis（结束、界限），核心义「到达尽头」。

sensesIntro.cn: finish 意为完成、结束、终点或表面处理。

core.en: Reaching the end of a task or object.
core.cn: 到达任务或物体的尽头。

branches.en: Doing the last step of a task.
An event reaching its end.
The final point itself.
The final treatment of a surface.
The action and the place share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与位置共用一个词。

intro.en: Finish grows from the Latin root finis through French and English suffixes.
intro.cn: finish 从拉丁词根 finis 出发，经由法语和英语后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: The Latin finis and finire also gave final, finance, and define.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 与 finire 也孕育了 final、finance 和 define。

items.example: I will finish the report tonight.
An unfinished painting stood on the easel.
items.exampleCN: 画架上放着一幅未完成的画。
他们给旧地板重新做了表面处理。

definition_zh: 消防员；司炉工

core_image: 浓烟里，一个戴头盔的身影抱着水带向前冲

senses.title: Firefighter
senses.definition: a person whose job is to put out dangerous fires
senses.definitionCN: 以扑灭危险火灾为职业的人
senses.example: The fireman rushed into the smoke to save people.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员冲进浓烟里去救人。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代主要的义项。

senses.title: Stoker
senses.definition: a person who tends the fire in a furnace or engine
senses.definitionCN: 负责照看炉子或发动机炉火的人
senses.example: The fireman shoveled coal into the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 司炉工把煤铲进发动机的炉膛。
senses.why: Steam engines needed someone to feed the fire.
senses.whyCN: 蒸汽机需要有人不断添火。

intro.en: Fireman is a plain compound of fire and man, first used for anyone who tended a fire.
intro.cn: fireman 是 fire 与 man 的直白复合词，最初指照看炉火的人。

items.en: Fyr and mann were separate words.
items.cn: fyr 与 mann 原本是两个独立的词。

items.en: Fireman named a stoker or furnace tender.
items.cn: fireman 指司炉工或看炉人。

items.en: Fireman came to mean a firefighter.
items.cn: fireman 逐渐指消防员。

items.en: Firefighter became the neutral term.
items.cn: firefighter 成为更中性的说法。

items.en: Fireman is still common in everyday speech.
items.cn: fireman 在日常口语中仍很常见。

note.en: Fireman is compared with similar-looking words and with words for rescuers.

entries.definition: a person who puts out fires

normalIntro.en: Fireman literally joins fire and man: a man who works with fire.
normalIntro.cn: fireman 字面上就是 fire 加 man：与火打交道的男人。

normal.en: The fireman carried a long ladder.
normal.cn: 消防员扛着长梯。

normal.en: A fireman wears a heavy helmet.
normal.cn: 消防员戴着沉重的头盔。

normal.en: The fireman checked every room.
normal.cn: 消防员检查了每个房间。

normal.en: An old fireman fed the steam engine.
normal.cn: 一位老司炉工给蒸汽机添煤。

normal.en: Firemen train to move through smoke.
normal.cn: 消防员训练在浓烟中行动。

abstract.en: Some people run toward what others flee.
abstract.cn: 有些人奔向别人逃离的地方。

abstract.en: A helmet hides a face but not a purpose.
abstract.cn: 头盔遮住面容，却遮不住使命。

abstract.en: To tend a fire is to keep a machine alive.
abstract.cn: 照看炉火，就是让机器继续活着。

examples.en: The fireman rushed into the smoke to save people.
examples.cn: 消防员冲进浓烟里去救人。

examples.en: The fireman climbed the ladder to the roof.
examples.cn: 消防员顺着梯子爬上屋顶。

examples.en: The fireman shoveled coal into the engine.
examples.cn: 司炉工把煤铲进发动机的炉膛。

sensesIntro.en: Fireman means a firefighter or a person who tends a furnace fire.
sensesIntro.cn: fireman 意为消防员或司炉工。

core.en: A person whose work is bound to fire.
core.cn: 工作与火紧密相连的人。

branches.en: One who puts out fires.

branches.cn: 两者都直接与火打交道。

definition_en: relating to government money, especially taxes and public spending

senses.title: Relating to government revenue and spending
senses.titleCN: 与政府收入及支出有关
senses.definition: concerning the money a government raises through taxes and spends on public needs
senses.definitionCN: 关于政府以税收取得、并用于公共需要的钱
senses.example: The fiscal cost of the programme was spread over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的财政成本被分摊到十年之间。
senses.why: the word descends from the Latin word for a money basket, so whatever is fiscal belongs to the public purse rather than a private one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词上溯拉丁语中「钱筐」的说法，因此凡是财政的，都属公家钱袋而非私人钱包。

senses.title: The twelve-month accounting period
senses.titleCN: 财政年度这一十二个月的账期
senses.definition: the year a government or firm uses for budgeting and accounts, which need not begin in January
senses.definitionCN: 政府或企业用于预算与记账的年度，未必从一月开始
senses.example: The fiscal year closes at the end of March for many public bodies.
senses.exampleCN: 许多公共机构的财政年度在三月底结束。
senses.why: because accounts must be closed somewhere, the adjective attaches to the period chosen, giving a fixed label to an arbitrary calendar span.
senses.whyCN: 账目总要在某处结清，这个形容词于是附着在被选定的期间上，为一个任意的日历跨度提供固定标签。

senses.title: The balance of the public budget
senses.definition: describing whether a government is running a surplus, a balance or a deficit
senses.definitionCN: 描述政府处于盈余、平衡还是赤字状态
senses.example: The country entered the crisis with a fiscal surplus of two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该国带着相当于经济总量百分之二的财政盈余进入危机。
senses.why: once taxes and spending are counted, the difference is a fact about the public purse, so the adjective names the state of that balance.
senses.whyCN: 税收与支出算清之后，差额成为公家钱袋的事实，这个形容词便指该差额的状态。

senses.title: Fiscal discipline and restraint
senses.definition: the practice of keeping spending and borrowing inside agreed limits
senses.definitionCN: 把支出与借款保持在约定限度内的做法
senses.example: Fiscal discipline required the ministry to refuse the extra request.
senses.exampleCN: 财政纪律要求该部拒绝这笔额外申请。
senses.why: the word can be pressed into service as a norm, not only a description, which is why it appears beside discipline and restraint.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以被当作规范使用，而不只是描述，因此常与纪律、约束一类词并置。

senses.title: Fiscal stimulus by spending or cutting tax
senses.titleCN: 以增支或减税作财政刺激
senses.definition: a deliberate expansion of the budget to raise demand during a slowdown
senses.definitionCN: 在放缓时期有意扩大预算以提高需求
senses.example: The fiscal stimulus arrived late but was large enough to shorten the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 财政刺激来得迟，但规模足以缩短衰退。
senses.why: when private demand falls, the public budget can take its place for a season, so extra spending is the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 私人需求下滑时，公共预算可以暂时替代它，额外支出于是成为工具。

senses.title: The fiscal burden on taxpayers
senses.titleCN: 纳税人承受的财政负担
senses.definition: the weight of taxes and contributions that households and firms must carry
senses.definitionCN: 家庭与企业必须承担的税收与缴费之重
senses.example: Officials argued that the fiscal burden already discouraged hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 官员认为财政负担已经在抑制招聘。
senses.why: every tax is a claim on private income, so the same budget that funds services also weighs on those who pay.
senses.whyCN: 每一项税都是对私人收入的索取，因此供给公共服务的同一预算也压在被征者身上。

senses.title: A revenue stamp or fiscal mark
senses.definition: an official stamp showing that a tax on a document has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 表明某份文书已缴税的官方印花
senses.example: The deed carried a fiscal stamp in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据的角上贴着财政印花。
senses.why: taxing papers required a visible proof of payment, so the adjective came to name the mark as well as the treasury behind it.
senses.whyCN: 对文书征税需要看得见的缴款凭证，这个形容词于是既指国库，也指那个印记。

senses.title: A public prosecutor in some legal systems
senses.definition: the official who prosecutes on behalf of the state, as in Scots and Spanish practice
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家提起公诉的官员，如苏格兰与西班牙的用法
senses.example: The fiscal presented the evidence to the court.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官向法庭提交了证据。
senses.why: the prosecutor was originally the treasury's lawyer, so the same word for the purse produced a title for the state's advocate.
senses.whyCN: 检察官最初是国库的律师，因此同一个表示钱袋的词也产出了国家公诉人的头衔。

intro.en: Fiscal comes from Latin fiscalis 'of the fiscus', the basket or chest that held public money. English borrowed it through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fiscal 来自拉丁 fiscalis「属于 fiscus 的」，fiscus 原指盛公款的篮子或钱箱。英语于 16 世纪经法语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fiscus first meant a woven basket, then the chest in which the Roman treasury kept its money, and finally the treasury itself as an institution.
items.cn: fiscus 先指编织的篮子，后指罗马国库存放钱款的钱箱，最后指作为机构的国库本身。

items.en: The adjective fiscalis 'of the treasury' described officials, taxes and property belonging to the public chest rather than to the emperor's private purse.
items.cn: 形容词 fiscalis「国库的」描述属于公家钱箱而非皇帝私产的官员、税收与财物。

items.en: Old French fiscal carried the word into English in the sixteenth century, at first in legal writing about the royal treasury.
items.cn: 古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪把这个词带进英语，最初见于关于王室国库的法律文书。

items.en: By the eighteenth century fiscal was used broadly for taxes, debt and budgeting, and the phrase fiscal year took its modern meaning in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，fiscal 已广泛用于税收、债务与预算；「财政年度」一语在 19 世纪取得现代含义。

items.en: In legal systems where the state's advocate acted for the treasury, fiscal became a title for the public prosecutor, a sense still current in Scotland and Spain.
items.cn: 在国家公诉人代国库行事的法系中，fiscal 成为检察官的头衔，这一义在苏格兰与西班牙仍在使用。

items.en: The revenue stamp sense arose because a taxed document needed a visible mark, so the adjective named the proof of payment as well as the office behind it.
items.cn: 印花义的产生，是因为被征税的文书需要看得见的标记，形容词于是既指缴款凭证，也指其背后的机关。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the treasury root or the same budget field; group two holds adjectives that are often used where fiscal belongs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「国库」词根或同属预算领域的形近词；第二组是常被用在 fiscal 位置上的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The treasury or public purse itself, an archaic noun; fiscal describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国库或公家钱袋本身，是古旧名词；fiscal 描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: In financial terms, especially of public money; it modifies an action rather than naming a field.
entries.definitionCN: 指从财政角度，尤指公款；它修饰动作，而非命名领域。

entries.definition: To take property into the public chest as a penalty; the root is the same money basket.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为处罚把财物收进公家钱箱；词根正是那只钱筐。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to matter, from a different Greek root; it shares only a sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体的或物质的，出自另一希腊词根；仅读音相近。

entries.definition: Relating to money and finance in general, including private firms; fiscal is reserved for public money.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指金钱与金融，包含私人企业；fiscal 专指公款。

entries.definition: Relating to money supply and currency; fiscal concerns taxing and spending by the government.
entries.definitionCN: 指货币供应与通货；fiscal 关乎政府的征税与支出。

entries.definition: Relating to a budget as a plan; fiscal can describe the whole year's accounts and the treasury behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为计划的预算；fiscal 可以描述整年账目及其背后的国库。

entries.definition: Relating to money as a medium, often in legal writing about loss; it lacks the public-purse sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为媒介的金钱，常用于关于损失的法律文书；不含公家钱袋义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The basket is still inside the word: a woven chest where the state keeps its money.
normal.cn: 那只篮子仍在词里：国家存钱的编织箱。

normal.en: The family runs fisc, fiscal, fiscally, confiscate, confiscation, fiscal year.
normal.cn: 同族词包括国库、财政的、在财政上、没收、充公、财政年度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the budget: fiscal year, fiscal deficit, fiscal discipline, fiscal stimulus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出预算的各个方面：财政年度、财政赤字、财政纪律、财政刺激。

normal.en: Confiscate is the same root used as a penalty: the property goes into the public chest.
normal.cn: 没收是同一词根用作处罚：财物被收进公家钱箱。

normal.en: In Scotland a fiscal is a prosecutor because the state's lawyer once acted for the treasury.
normal.cn: 在苏格兰，检察官也被叫作这个词，因为国家律师曾代国库行事。

abstract.en: Picture one chest with a tax bill going in at the top and a road coming out at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱箱，上面进税单，下面出一条公路。

abstract.en: Picture a household calendar whose year ends in March, not December.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，年份在三月底而非十二月底结束。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp in the corner of a deed, small but able to stop a sale.
abstract.cn: 想象契据角上的一枚印花，虽小却能拦住一笔买卖。

examples.en: The fiscal cost of the war outlasted the fighting by a generation.
examples.cn: 这场战争的财政代价在战事结束后还延续了一代人。

examples.en: Fiscal rules were tightened after the deficit exceeded the legal limit.
examples.cn: 赤字超过法定上限后，财政规则被收紧。

examples.en: The fiscal year ends in June, so the accounts close before the summer recess.
examples.cn: 财政年度在六月结束，账目在夏季休会前结清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「钱筐」——公家把钱装进筐里，进的是税、出的是公共开支 → 财政的

root: 拉丁 fiscus 原指编织篮，后指罗马国库的钱箱，再指国库机构；形容词 fiscalis「国库的」经古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪入英语。同根词有 confiscate、confiscation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chest: what goes into it, the year it is counted over, the balance left at the end, the discipline of not overdrawing it, extra spending in a slump, the weight on those who fill it, the stamp that proves a tax was paid, and the lawyer who once spoke for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一只钱箱：装进去的东西、按什么年度结账、年终剩下的差额、不透支的纪律、衰退时的额外支出、向填箱者施加的重量、证明缴税的印花，以及曾替它说话的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public chest with a tax bill entering at the top and a public work leaving at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只公家钱箱，上面进税单，下面出公共工程。

branches.en: THE PURSE AND ITS WEIGHT: what belongs to the chest, and what it costs those who fill it.
branches.cn: 钱袋与重量：属于钱箱的东西，以及填箱者为此付出的代价。

branches.en: THE COUNTING PERIOD: a chosen twelve months in which income and outgo are closed off.
branches.cn: 结算期间：被选定的十二个月，在此之内结清收入与支出。

branches.en: BALANCE AND DISCIPLINE: the difference at year end, and the rule against overdrawing it.
branches.cn: 差额与纪律：年终的差额，以及不得透支的规则。

branches.en: DELIBERATE EXPANSION: in a slump the chest is opened wider on purpose.
branches.cn: 有意扩张：衰退时故意把钱箱开得更大。

branches.en: PROOF AND ADVOCATE: the stamp proves the tax was paid, and the prosecutor once spoke for the chest.
branches.cn: 凭证与代言人：印花证明税已缴，检察官曾替钱箱说话。

intro.en: Fiscal is a Latin adjective from the word for the public money chest; the root also gives the verb for taking property into that chest.
intro.cn: fiscal 是由「公家钱箱」一词派生的拉丁形容词；同一词根还给出「把财物收进钱箱」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fiscus and fiscalis stand behind fiscal, fisc and confiscate; the basket is the common image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fiscus 与 fiscalis 支撑 fiscal、fisc 与 confiscate；那只篮子是他们共同的意象。

senses.why: A body in good shape is fit.
senses.whyCN: 状态良好的身体就是 fit。

senses.title: Right size
senses.definition: to be the right size or shape for someone
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或形状正好适合某人
senses.example: This pair of shoes fits well.
senses.exampleCN: 这双鞋很合脚。
senses.why: Clothing is the everyday testing ground.
senses.whyCN: 衣服是这个词最常见的测试场。

senses.title: To suit
senses.definition: to be suitable for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 适合某事或某人
senses.example: The job fits her skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作适合她的技能。
senses.why: What matches a need fits it.
senses.whyCN: 与需求相匹配，就是适合。

senses.title: To install
senses.definition: to put a part or device into place
senses.definitionCN: 把部件或装置放到正确位置
senses.example: They fitted a new lock.
senses.exampleCN: 他们装了一把新锁。
senses.why: A part that fits is placed in place.
senses.whyCN: 能贴合的部分被安置到位。

intro.en: Fit appeared in late Middle English with the sense of matching or being suited; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: fit 出现在中古英语晚期，意为「相配、适合」，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Fit meant a match or a contest.
items.cn: fit 指匹配或较量。

items.en: Fit came to mean suited or proper.
items.cn: fit 引申为适合的、恰当的。

items.en: Fit described clothing that matches the body.
items.cn: fit 描述衣服与身体相合。

items.en: Fit meant healthy and in good condition.
items.cn: fit 意为健康、状态良好。

items.en: The verb named the placing of a part.
items.cn: 动词形式指把部件安装到位。

note.en: Fit is compared with similar-looking words and with words for suitability and health.
note.cn: 把 fit 与形近词以及表示适合和健康的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fit links a good match: clothes that match the body, work that matches skills, a part that matches its place.
normalIntro.cn: fit 连接着各种「相配」：衣服配身体、工作配技能、零件配位置。

normal.en: These shoes fit perfectly.
normal.cn: 这双鞋非常合脚。

normal.en: Exercise keeps you fit.
normal.cn: 锻炼让你保持健康。

normal.en: The key fits the lock.
normal.cn: 这把钥匙配这把锁。

normal.en: He fits in well at school.
normal.cn: 他在学校适应得很好。

normal.en: They fitted new windows.
normal.cn: 他们装了新窗户。

abstract.en: To fit is to find the place where something belongs.
abstract.cn: 适合，就是找到某物所属的位置。

abstract.en: A healthy body and a proper word share the same name.
abstract.cn: 健康的身体与恰当的词，共用一个名字。

abstract.en: What fits does not need force.
abstract.cn: 真正合适的东西，不需要硬塞。

examples.en: This pair of shoes fits well.
examples.cn: 这双鞋很合脚。

examples.en: She runs to keep fit.
examples.cn: 她跑步以保持健康。

examples.en: They fitted a new lock.
examples.cn: 他们装了一把新锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: fit 是中古英语晚期出现的词，核心义「相配、合适」，后引申出健康与安装。

root: 源自中古英语 fit（相配、较量），更深来源不确定，核心义「恰好相合」。

sensesIntro.en: Fit means suitable, healthy, right in size, suited to something, or to install.
sensesIntro.cn: fit 意为合适的、健康的、合身、适合或安装。

core.en: A match between a thing and its purpose or place.
core.cn: 事物与其用途或位置之间的契合。

branches.en: Right for a purpose.
A body in good condition.
Clothing of the right size.
A match of skills and tasks.
A part placed where it belongs.
branches.cn: 零件被安放到应在的位置。

intro.en: Fit is a short Middle English word that forms many everyday compounds.
intro.cn: fit 是中古英语的短词，构成了许多日常复合词。

latinIntro.en: Fit has no Latin ancestor; Latin aptus, fitted, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fit 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 aptus（合适的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: It was a fitting end to the day.
items.exampleCN: 这是这一天恰如其分的结尾。

items.example: The water is unfit to drink.

items.exampleCN: 她穿了一身亮眼的衣服。

definition_zh: 适应度；健康；体能；适合
definition_en: the state of being physically healthy, the quality of being suitable, or in biology the relative reproductive success of a variant
core_image: 一只体态匀称的鹿站在坡上，旁边画着后代数量刻度与心率曲线，背景有哑铃剪影
scene: 同一片草场上有三只同种甲虫，各自留下的后代数量差了三倍。Reproductive fitness is measured not by how long an insect lives but by how many of its young survive.
sceneCN: 这里 fitness 指「（生殖）适应度」（第 3 个义项：个体在下一代基因库中所占的相对贡献）；句意：生殖适应度不看昆虫活多久，而看它有多少后代存活。图中可辨识物件：同种甲虫、后代数量刻度、存活率曲线、草场样方。

pos.zh: 健康；体能；适合；适应度（多为不可数）

derivatives.zh: 健康的；合适的 / 适合；安装

senses.title: Physical condition
senses.definition: the condition of being physically healthy and strong
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康、有力的状态
senses.example: Regular hill walking improved his fitness within a season.
senses.exampleCN: 经常走山路使他的体能在一个季节内提高。
senses.why: fit first meant 'suited, well matched', and a body suited to its tasks came to be called fit.
senses.whyCN: fit 最初意为「合适的、匹配良好的」，适合其任务的身体便被称为 fit。

senses.title: Suitability or match
senses.definition: the quality of being suitable for a purpose or a position
senses.definitionCN: 适合某用途或某职位的性质
senses.example: The fitness of the site for a wetland was assessed first.
senses.exampleCN: 首先评估了该地块作为湿地的适合性。
senses.why: this is the oldest branch: a thing fits a slot, and its fittingness is its fitness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一支：一物契合一个位置，其契合程度就是它的适合性。

senses.title: Evolutionary fitness
senses.titleCN: 进化适应度：后代的相对贡献
senses.definition: in biology, an individual's relative contribution of offspring to the next generation
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中个体对下一代基因库的相对后代贡献
senses.example: Fitness is measured relative to other individuals, not on an absolute scale.
senses.exampleCN: 适应度是相对于其他个体测量的，而非绝对尺度。
senses.why: biology took the 'goodness of fit' idea and made it about fit between organism and environment, expressed as offspring.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「契合度」的概念，把它用于生物与环境之间的匹配，并以后代数量表达。

senses.title: Inclusive fitness
senses.titleCN: 广义适合度：含亲属的后代
senses.definition: the fitness gained through one's own offspring plus the offspring helped in relatives
senses.definitionCN: 由自身后代加上帮助亲属所增后代构成的适合度
senses.example: Helpers at the nest raise the inclusive fitness of their siblings.
senses.exampleCN: 巢边的帮手提高了其手足的广义适合度。
senses.why: once shared genes matter, helping a relative counts as part of one's own reproductive score.
senses.whyCN: 一旦共享基因被计入，帮助亲属也算进自身的繁殖得分。

senses.title: Fitness landscape
senses.titleCN: 适应度地形：把适合度画成山丘
senses.definition: a model that maps genotypes or traits onto reproductive success as a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把基因型或性状映射为繁殖成功的曲面模型
senses.example: The population climbed a local peak on the fitness landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 该群体在适应度地形上爬上一座局部山峰。
senses.why: the abstract score becomes a shape that can be walked, so peaks and valleys stand for good and poor combinations.
senses.whyCN: 抽象分数变成一个可行走的形状，峰与谷代表好与差的组合。

senses.title: Fitness testing and training
senses.titleCN: 体测与健身：日常健康语境
senses.definition: the everyday use for measured physical capacity and for gym training
senses.definitionCN: 日常语境中指可测量的身体能力与健身训练
senses.example: The team ran a fitness test before the season began.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季开始前球队做了体能测试。
senses.why: sport fixed the word to measurable capacity such as endurance and strength.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词固定到可测量的能力上，如耐力与力量。

senses.title: Statistical goodness of fit
senses.titleCN: 统计拟合优度：模型与数据的贴合
senses.definition: in statistics, how well a model or curve matches observed data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中模型或曲线与观测数据的贴合程度
senses.example: The fitness of the model was poor at high temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在高温下的拟合优度很差。
senses.why: the same 'fit' is used for a curve fitting points, with no biological content at all.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 fit 也用于曲线贴合数据点，完全不含生物学内容。

senses.title: Suitability for a post or role
senses.definition: the quality of being qualified for a role or office
senses.definitionCN: 胜任某角色或职位的资格
senses.example: The committee questioned his fitness for the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会质疑他是否适合担任主席。
senses.why: institutional life keeps the oldest sense alive: fitness is fitness for something named.
senses.whyCN: 制度生活保留了最古老的义项：适合性总是对某个被命名的东西而言。

intro.en: Fitness is fit plus -ness. The adjective fit has an uncertain origin, and the biological sense was fixed in the nineteenth century. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: fitness 由 fit 加 -ness 构成。形容词 fit 的来源不确定，生物学义在 19 世纪固定下来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Fit appears in the thirteenth to fourteenth centuries meaning 'suitable, well matched'; its earlier origin is uncertain, and no source is agreed.
items.cn: fit 于 13 至 14 世纪出现，意为「合适的、匹配良好的」；其更早来源不确定，学界没有一致结论。

items.en: A separate noun fit meant a bout or a song, and some dictionaries suspect a link with the adjective; this remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated source.
items.cn: 另有一个名词 fit 指一阵发作或一首歌，部分词典怀疑它与形容词有关；这仍属假说，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: Fitness is recorded in the sixteenth century as 'suitableness', before any health sense.
items.cn: fitness 于 16 世纪有记录，意为「合适」，早于任何健康义。

items.en: The 'physical condition' sense grows in the nineteenth century with organised sport and gymnasium culture.
items.cn: 「体能」义随 19 世纪有组织的体育与健身房文化而发展。

items.en: Darwin and Spencer made fitness a technical measure of reproductive success, later formalised as relative genetic contribution.
items.cn: 达尔文与斯宾塞把 fitness 变成繁殖成功的术语指标，后来形式化为相对基因贡献。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-English origin of fit is unknown, and any reconstructed form offered for it is speculative.
items.cn: 来源不确定：fit 在英语之前的来源不明，凡为它给出的重构形式均属推测。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the fit family and its homographs; group two holds measures and near terms from biology and sport.
note.cn: 第一组是 fit 词族及同形词的形近词；第二组是生物学与体育中的指标与近义词。

entries.definition: Healthy, suitable, or to make something match. Fitness is the noun of state built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指健康的、合适的，或使某物相配；fitness 是由它构成的状态名词。

entries.definition: Either 'suitable' or the act of trying on clothes. It is not the biological measure.
entries.definitionCN: 或指「恰当的」，或指试衣；它不是生物学指标。

entries.definition: Not healthy or not suitable, the direct negation of fit.
entries.definitionCN: 指不健康或不合适，是 fit 的直接否定。

entries.definition: An old spelling of fitness found in sixteenth-century texts; it is the same word, not a variant sense.
entries.definitionCN: 16 世纪文本中的旧拼法；是同一个词，并非另一义项。

entries.definition: The same biological measure spelled out: relative contribution of offspring. It avoids confusion with gym fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 同一生物学指标的完整说法：后代的相对贡献；可避免与健身义混淆。

entries.definition: General physical and mental well-being. It is not a relative measure and carries no genetic meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体的身心安好；不是相对指标，也不含遗传含义。

entries.definition: The state of a body or machine, often used in sport for endurance. It is broader than fitness and less measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机器的状态，体育中常指耐力；比 fitness 更宽泛、更少量化。

entries.definition: A fitted trait. Fitness is the reproductive score that such traits tend to raise.
entries.definitionCN: 指适应出来的性状；fitness 是这类性状往往会提高的繁殖得分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fit 'suited' + -ness 'state': the state of being well matched.
normal.cn: fit「合适的」+ -ness「状态」：匹配良好的状态。

normal.en: The family runs fit, fitness, fitting, unfit, fitly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fit、fitness、fitting、unfit、fitly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: physical fitness, fitness test, reproductive fitness, fitness landscape.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：体能、体能测试、生殖适应度、适应度地形。

normal.en: In biology, always ask what fitness is relative to; it has no absolute zero.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，总要问适应度是相对于谁；它没有绝对零点。

normal.en: Do not read reproductive fitness as physical health; the two senses are far apart.
normal.cn: 不要把生殖适应度读成身体健康；这两个义项相距很远。

abstract.en: Picture a key that turns smoothly in one lock and jams in another.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在一把锁里顺滑转动，在另一把里卡住。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard that counts surviving young instead of years lived.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌数的是存活后代而不是寿命。

abstract.en: Picture a hill map where each step uphill means more offspring.
abstract.cn: 想象一张山丘地图，每向上一步就意味着更多后代。

examples.en: Fitness in evolutionary biology is always relative to the rest of the population.
examples.cn: 进化生物学中的适应度总是相对于群体其余个体而言。

examples.en: Her fitness improved after three months of swimming.
examples.cn: 游了三个月后，她的体能提高了。

examples.en: The model's fitness to the data was tested at five sites.
examples.cn: 这个模型对数据的拟合优度在五个地点接受了检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥（fit）得合适」——身子合适叫健康，基因合适叫适应度 → 体能、适合、适应度

root: 英语 fit「合适的」+ -ness；fit 的英语之前来源不确定（相关假说均未证实）；生物学义由达尔文与斯宾塞在 19 世纪固定为繁殖成功的相对指标。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: being well matched, whether a body to its tasks, a word to a post, an organism to its habitat, a relative's genes to yours, a model to data, or a curve to points.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：匹配良好——身体与任务、人与职位、生物与生境、亲属基因与你、模型与数据、曲线与数据点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that fits its work, with offspring counted beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副与工作相合的身体，旁边记着后代数量。

branches.en: BODY: health and measured capacity are the everyday face of being fit.
branches.cn: 身体：健康与可测能力是「合适」的日常面孔。

branches.en: SUITABILITY: the oldest sense, fitness for a purpose, a site or a post.
branches.cn: 适合性：最古老的义项，对用途、地块或职位的适合。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: fitness becomes a relative count of descendants, own and shared.
branches.cn: 繁殖：适应度变成后代数量的相对计数，含自身与共享部分。

branches.en: MODEL: the score is drawn as a landscape of peaks and valleys.
branches.cn: 模型：得分被画成峰谷起伏的地形。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the same word measures how well a curve fits data.
branches.cn: 统计：同一个词衡量曲线与数据的贴合程度。

intro.en: Fitness is a short English adjective plus the native noun suffix -ness; it has no Latin affix structure of its own.
intro.cn: fitness 是简短英语形容词加本族名词后缀 -ness；它本身没有拉丁词缀结构。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin family; its relatives are English formations such as fitting, unfit and fitly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词族；其同族词是 fitting、unfit、fitly 等英语构词。

items.example: The seed is fit for dispersal by wind.
items.exampleCN: 这粒种子适合随风传播。

items.example: A fitting end to the dry season was a gentle rain.
items.exampleCN: 旱季的一个恰当收尾是一场细雨。

items.example: The wet field was unfit for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 湿透的田地不适合放牧。

items.example: The hut was fitly placed above the flood line.
items.exampleCN: 小屋恰当地建在洪水线之上。

items.example: The lighter seeds are fitter for wind travel.
items.exampleCN: 更轻的种子更适合随风传播。

items.example: The boat was refitted for the survey.
items.exampleCN: 这条船为调查重新装配。

items.example: The field outfit included nets and jars.

definition_zh: 修理；解决；固定；确定
definition_en: to repair something, to solve a problem, to fasten something in place, or to decide something firmly
core_image: 拧紧松动的螺丝，让摇晃的椅子重新站稳
scene: 他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。He spent the afternoon fixing the wobbly chair.
sceneCN: 这里 fix 是「修理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他花了一下午修好了那把摇晃的椅子。

senses.title: Repair
senses.definition: to make something whole or working again
senses.definitionCN: 使某物恢复完整或正常运转
senses.example: He fixed the wobbly chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他修好了那把摇晃的椅子。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of fixing a broken object.
senses.whyCN: 这是修理损坏物品时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Solve
senses.definition: to find a solution to a problem
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到解决办法
senses.example: They fixed the problem in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一小时就解决了问题。
senses.why: A problem is treated like a machine that needs repair.
senses.whyCN: 问题被当作需要修理的机器来对待。

senses.title: Fasten
senses.definition: to attach something firmly in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: The shelf is fixed to the wall with screws.
senses.exampleCN: 架子用螺丝固定在墙上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is driving something in until it cannot move.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西钉进去使其不能移动。

senses.title: Arrange firmly
senses.definition: to decide or arrange something definitely
senses.definitionCN: 把某事明确地决定或安排好
senses.example: We fixed a date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们确定了会议的日期。
senses.why: Something fixed is no longer open to change.
senses.whyCN: 被固定下来的事就不再变动了。

intro.en: Fix comes from Latin figere, to fasten or drive in, through its participle fixus.
intro.cn: fix 源自拉丁语 figere（钉住、固定），经其分词 fixus 进入英语。

items.en: Figere meant to drive in or fasten.
items.cn: figere 意为钉入或固定。

items.en: The participle fixus meant fastened or fixed.
items.cn: 分词 fixus 意为被固定住的。

items.en: Fixare meant to fasten or settle something.
items.cn: fixare 意为使固定、使确定。

items.en: Fix named fastening and then repairing.
items.cn: fix 先指固定，后指修理。

items.en: The word also came to mean solving or arranging.
items.cn: 这个词又引申为解决或安排。

note.en: Fix is compared with similar-looking words and with words for repair and fastening.
note.cn: 把 fix 与形近词以及表示修理和固定的词作比较。

entries.definition: a wild animal with a bushy tail
to repair a hole or tear

normalIntro.en: Fix means to make firm: you fasten it, then you make it work again.
normalIntro.cn: fix 的核心是「使牢固」：先固定，再让它恢复正常。

normal.en: You fix a broken chair.
normal.cn: 你修理一把坏椅子。

normal.en: You fix a problem at work.
normal.cn: 你解决工作中的问题。

normal.en: You fix a shelf to the wall.
normal.cn: 你把架子固定在墙上。

normal.en: You fix a date for a trip.
normal.cn: 你确定旅行的日期。

normal.en: A fixed price never changes.
normal.cn: 固定价格不会变。

abstract.en: To fix is to stop something from shaking.
abstract.cn: 修理就是让某物不再摇晃。

abstract.en: A fixed point makes movement measurable.
abstract.cn: 固定的参照点让运动可以被衡量。

abstract.en: Some things are easier to fix than to explain.
abstract.cn: 有些东西修起来比解释起来容易。

examples.en: Can you fix the leaking tap?
examples.cn: 你能修一下漏水的水龙头吗？

examples.en: They fixed the date for the wedding.
examples.cn: 他们确定了婚礼的日期。

examples.en: The mirror is fixed to the wall.
examples.cn: 镜子固定在墙上。

dict_mnemonic.text: fix 源自拉丁语 figere（钉住），本义「固定」，故障被「固定」回正常状态就是修理。

root: 源自拉丁语 figere（钉入、固定），核心义「使牢固不动」。

sensesIntro.en: Fix means to repair, to solve, to fasten, or to settle something firmly.
sensesIntro.cn: fix 意为修理、解决、固定或把某事确定下来。

core.en: To make something firm and no longer loose.
core.cn: 使某物牢固、不再松动。

branches.en: A broken thing made whole again.
branches.cn: 把损坏的东西恢复完整。

branches.en: A problem settled like a loose part.
branches.cn: 像拧紧零件一样解决问题。

branches.en: An object held firmly in place.
A decision made firm and final.
branches.cn: 把决定敲定得稳固而最终。

branches.en: Repair and fastening share the idea of firmness.
branches.cn: 修理与固定共享「牢固」这一概念。

intro.en: Fix belongs to a Latin family built on figere, to fasten.
intro.cn: fix 属于以拉丁语 figere（固定）为核心构建的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin figere and its participle fixus supply the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figere 及其分词 fixus 提供了整个词族。

items.example: He fixes cars for a living.
He fixated on one small detail.
items.exampleCN: 他盯住一个小细节不放。

latinEntries.example: The Latin verb figere meant to fasten.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语动词 figere 意为固定。

latinEntries.example: Fixus is the participle of figere.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fixus 是 figere 的分词。
